title: Why Belgium exists
episode: Why is Belgium a country? - History of Belgium in 11 Minutes
description: An animated history of the lands that became Belgium, from the rich medieval cities of Flanders to independence in 1830. Bruges’s Gothic city hall, begun in 1376, is one of the oldest in the Low Countries.

title: The best-preserved medieval city
episode: Secrets Of The Best Preserved Medieval City In Europe | Curious Traveler | Absolute History
description: A documentary on how Bruges became a trading city linked to the Hanseatic League, and why it looks so medieval today. After its harbor silted up, the city was too poor to rebuild, so its old buildings survived.

title: The van Eyck brothers
episode: The Mysterious Tale of the Van Eyck Family (Art History Documentary)
description: Art critic Waldemar Januszczak on Jan van Eyck, who painted for the Duke of Burgundy and lived in Bruges until his death in 1441, and his mysterious brother Hubert. A statue of Jan stands on the square named after him.

title: A painting you can step into
episode: Jan van Eyck, The Virgin and Child with Canon Joris van der Paele
description: Two art historians look closely at Jan van Eyck’s painting of a Bruges canon kneeling before the Virgin, painted in 1436. They point out the details: the canon’s glasses, his wrinkles, and the reflection in a saint’s armor.

title: Books of Hours
episode: Medieval Books of Hours in the Public Library of Bruges
description: The city library shows its illuminated Books of Hours, private prayer books that Bruges workshops made and sold across Europe in the 1400s. The library still holds hundreds of medieval manuscripts.

title: The beguines
description: A talk on the beguines, medieval women who lived together in religious communities without taking vows. They could leave, own property, and earn a living. The Bruges beguinage is now home to Benedictine nuns.

title: Michelangelo’s Madonna
description: A short look at the marble Madonna and Child in the Church of Our Lady. Nazi soldiers took it in 1944, and the Monuments Men, Allied officers who traced stolen art, brought it back after the war.

title: The beer pipeline
description: Tom Scott on the pipe that carries beer about two miles under the streets of Bruges, from the De Halve Maan brewery in the old center to its bottling plant outside the city. It was built in 2016 to get trucks off the cobbles.

title: The raid on Zeebrugge
episode: 200 Medals Won in an Hour - Raid on Zeebrugge 1918 Documentary
description: On April 23, 1918, St. George’s Day, the Royal Navy tried to block the harbor at Zeebrugge, which German U-boats used to reach the sea from their base in Bruges. Eight Victoria Crosses were awarded for the night.
